raw:
{
  "need": "Identity",
  "secondary": { "name": "Competence" },
  "read": "A new hire walking in Monday is actively asking themselves who they are in a professional context — what kind of worker, what kind of person, where they belong in the adult world. Before any standard is set, they are already scanning: will I be seen as capable and worth investing in, or just another body filling a seat? The identity question is front and center; competence sits right behind it because they do not yet know what good looks like here or whether they can pull it off.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Launch into a rules-and-expectations download on day one — here is how we do things, here is what is not acceptable, here are consequences — which signals distrust before they have done anything wrong and puts them on defense from the start." },
  "mentorMove": "Open by treating them as a developing professional whose perspective already matters, then layer in the standards as shared tools for their success — not a ceiling you are enforcing but a floor you are both standing on.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The standards themselves: quality of work, reliability, how we communicate when something goes sideways — none of those move.",
    "The expectation that they will ask questions and flag problems early rather than go quiet and hope it resolves itself."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "How they ramp up — the pace and sequence of early assignments can flex to match where they actually are.",
    "How they prefer to check in: standing one-on-one, a quick Slack at end of day, walking over — let them have a say in the method.",
    "How much context and background they need before diving in — some people want the big picture first, others want a concrete task; ask which helps them more."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, welcome — really glad you are here. Before we get into logistics, I want to say something I mean: I would not have pushed to hire you if I did not think you could do this job well. That belief is not going away." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "I have a few things I want to walk you through about how we work, but first I want to hear from you — what does a good first few weeks look like from your side? What would help you actually hit the ground running rather than just survive orientation?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I care about most: doing solid work, being straight with me when something is unclear or off track, and treating teammates well. Those are not negotiable. Everything else — how you structure your day, how we set up our check-ins, what you tackle first — I want your input on, because you are the one doing the work and you know things about how you operate that I do not." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am going to hold you to a high standard here, and I want you to know I am doing that because I genuinely think you can meet it — not to put pressure on you but because I think lowering the bar would actually be a disservice to you. What I need from you is this: when something is not clicking, you tell me before it becomes a problem. Can we agree on that?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "The first few weeks set the template for whether they will come to you when things get hard or hide it until it blows up — invest in building that honesty now and the rest of the year is significantly easier for both of you."
}
situation: A new hire starts Monday and I want to set clear expectations.
